item.title: Vanishing Theorem of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta Invariants as Stable Sections
item.description: arXiv:2611.13193v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a viewpoint of Pin(2)-equivariant Bauer-Furuta invariant: It can be converted to a section over a finite dimensional Pin(2)-orbit, and it takes values in ordinary stable homotopy class. This viewpoint reveals a topological limitation of the invariant: If the fiber's connectivity exceeds the dimension of the base space, then all sections are homotopic to the trivial section. We use it to recover Lin-Mukherjee vanishing theorem. Furthermore, the family Seiberg-Witten invariant can be obtained from the pullback of such sections to $S^1$-orbit. We use this fact to prove a vanishing theorem of the Pin(2)-equivariant family Bauer-Furuta invariant after two stabilizations.
item.dc:creator: Haochen Qiu

item.title: Thompson indices of knots and the invertibility problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.13208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jones showed that Thompson's group $F$ produces all unoriented links, and introduced its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}$, which produces all oriented links; the same holds for the Brown-Thompson group $F_3$ and its oriented subgroup $\vec{F}_3$. The corresponding Thompson indices measure the complexity of a knot in these groups, much as the braid index does for braid groups. In this article we prove that the span of the Jones polynomial plus $1$ is a lower bound for the $F$- and $\vec{F}$-index, and we give lower bounds for the $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index in terms of the degrees of the HOMFLY-PT polynomial. We then compute the four indices (the $F$-, $F_3$-, $\vec{F}$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index) for the prime knots with at most 13 crossings, by an exhaustive enumeration of tree diagrams (up to 13 leaves for $F$, 17 for $\vec{F}$, with the HOMFLY-PT polynomials of all the diagrams with 19 leaves, and 9 and 11 for $F_3$ and $\vec{F}_3$) completed by targeted searches; every value is rigorously certified, by exact computations and by verified computations of hyperbolic structures in interval arithmetic. The $F$-index is determined for all knots with at most 11 crossings, the $\vec{F}$-index for all knots with at most 8 crossings, and the $F_3$- and $\vec{F}_3$-index for all knots with at most 12 crossings. The main outcome of these computations is that the oriented indices are sensitive to the orientation: we find hundreds of non-invertible knots $K$ whose reverse $K^r$ has a different $\vec{F}$- or $\vec{F}_3$-index, the smallest being $8_{17}$ (with $\vec{F}_3$-index $7$ and $9$). The $\vec{F}$-index also distinguishes the Conway knot from its mutant, the Kinoshita-Terasaka knot.
item.dc:creator: Valeriano Aiello

item.title: Handlebody-links with Euler characteristic -2 up to six crossings
item.description: arXiv:2611.13302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We enumerate all non-split handlebody-links with Euler characteristic $-2$ up to six crossings, up to ambient isotopy and mirror image.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Bellettini, Giovanni Paolini, Maurizio Paolini, Yi-Sheng Wang

item.title: Every hyperbolic knot has an arc-faithful closed braid diagram
item.description: arXiv:2611.13305v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Every hyperbolic knot admits an arc-faithful closed braid diagram, answering Conjecture 29 of McPhail-Snyder. More precisely, any braid representing the knot can be reworded in the same braid group so that the complete holonomy has distinct incoming parabolic fixed points at every crossing. The construction replaces a pinched crossing by five non-pinched crossings when a suitable third strand is adjacent. On $n$ strands it uses at most $2n-1$ letters per replaced crossing. The resulting diagram realizes the complete holonomy by nondegenerate shapes in its four-term octahedral decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Haibin Hang

item.title: Genus zero simple knots
item.description: arXiv:2611.13440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify the simple knots in lens spaces with planar rational Seifert surfaces. As a consequence, we classify the homology classes of all knots in lens spaces that admit planar rational Seifert surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Evan Greene, Shiyu Liang, John Luecke

item.title: Surface subgroups with prescribed finite quotients
item.description: arXiv:2611.13458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every finite quotient of a finite covolume Kleinian group $G$ can be realized by a surface subgroup. More precisely, given an epimorphism from $G$ onto a finite group $F$, there exists a surface subgroup that maps surjectively onto $F$. As a consequence, the union of the surface subgroups is dense in $G$ with respect to the profinite topology. We also apply this result to obtain more examples of atoroidal surface bundles with signature zero in the construction of Kent--Leininger.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Fran\c{c}ois Lafont, Zhenghao Rao, Hongbin Sun

item.title: LLM-Assisted Advances in the Ropelength Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.14234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work summarizes some updates to the ropelength problem, concerning the shortest possible contour length of a unit-thickness knot, that were derived with the assistance of ChatGPT-5.6 Luna. The first of two main results is that the universal lower bound for a knot with crossing number C has been improved from $L\geq1.105C^{3/4}$ to $L\geq2.0996C^{3/4}$, achieved by further separating local and global terms in an optimization integral. The second main result is a bound relating ropelength to stick number (s), such that $L\geq\pi(s-1)$. This implies stronger lower bounds for the ropelengths of at least 41 torus knots, and a specific class of pretzel knots. Other results include an improved packing-based lower bound for T(Q,Q) links and an optimized standard parameterization for torus knots. There were many problems for which the LLM was unable to render assistance, for example in reducing the numerical coefficients or scalings of known universal upper bounds.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Klotz

item.title: Anosov representations from cyclic Higgs bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.14302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every complex simple Lie group G (not of type $E_8$) we construct the minimal Slodowy slice, which is a half-dimensional slice in the character variety of a closed surface group into G, containing the composition of Fuchsian representations with the minimal representation of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ in G and invariant under the mapping class group action. This slice is defined via cyclic Higgs bundles, and we show that when G is not of type $E_8$, the corresponding representations are Anosov, so in particular discrete and faithful, and dominate some Fuchsian representation. For each of these Higgs bundles, we consider the equivariant harmonic map to the symmetric space, and we show it is an embedding and a quasi-isometric embedding with regard to the induced metric. From the cyclicity of these Higgs bundles we are also able to construct an auxiliary harmonic map to a pseudoriemannian symmetric space $G/G^\sigma$ which is also an embedding. Our techniques also apply to harmonic Higgs bundles over the unit disk satisfying a certain completeness condition. These techniques also apply to two other families of cyclic Higgs bundles.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Bronstein, Colin Davalo, Qiongling Li

item.title: No 13-vertex triangulation of the three-torus
item.description: arXiv:2611.14367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: K\"uhnel and Lassmann constructed a neighborly triangulation of the three-torus on 15 vertices, and Lutz conjectured that it is vertex-minimal. The standard lower-bound arguments exclude at most twelve vertices but do not decide the 13- and 14-vertex cases. We exclude the 13-vertex case. Our proof uses the Novik--Swartz $g_2$-inequality and a simplicial-complement reduction to a nine-vertex model of the punctured three-torus. By analyzing fundamental groups of small simplicial complexes and applying Alexander duality in a vertex link, we obtain a contradiction from the deficiency of $\Z^3$.
item.dc:creator: Geunho Lim

item.title: Geometric Hammocks: Surface Laminations and the Ziegler Spectrum of String Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.12931v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give the first complete topological, geometric, and ergodic classification of the Ziegler spectrum $\Zg(\Lambda)$ of a non-domestic string algebra $\Lambda$ over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary cardinality, via a dictionary with Thurston's theory of geodesic laminations on a cusped hyperbolic surface. This is a model-theoretic counterpart of Haiden--Katzarkov--Kontsevich's realization (\emph{Publ.\ Math.\ IHES} 2017) of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of a gentle algebra via flat surfaces: pure-injective modules correspond to admissible geodesics, and the Ziegler topology to a corridor quotient of Chabauty space. Three consequences follow. The Krull--Gabriel dimension equals the surface's topological accumulation depth, and the string closure with all higher Cantor--Bendixson strata is globally homeomorphic to an explicit corridor space, with the pushout map to $\Zg(\Lambda)$ a homeomorphism if and only if $\Lambda$ is domestic. Prefix-free dyadic blocks in the geometric perfect core verify Puninski's cardinality-free two-chain criterion, resolving the open problem of superdecomposable pure-injectives over uncountable fields for all non-domestic string and special biserial algebras. Three purely algebraic invariants on the perfect core---localized pp-shape entropy, a $K_0$-weighted pressure function satisfying an algebraic Ruelle--Walters Variational Principle, and a pp-bifurcation index with a Gauss--Bonnet simplicity obstruction---strictly separate uncountable iso-entropic and iso-pressure families, and the inverse limit of the quotient pp-lattice recovers the transversal Cantor cross-section.
item.dc:creator: Shantanu Sardar

item.title: On the topology of some linear systems of hyperelliptic curves in Hirzebruch surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14386v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Following a program suggested by Dolgachev and Libgober in 1981, we study the topology of the locus of smooth sections of linear systems of hyperelliptic curves on Hirzebruch surfaces. Our primary interest is the computation of various flavors of ``enriched monodromy representations''. Within this class of examples, we find that a variety of behaviors occur - in some situations the enriched monodromy faithfully captures the fundamental group, and in others it does not. Our arguments mainly leverage algebro-geometric techniques to compute cohomological obstructions to families of embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Nick Salter

item.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We find \emph{exotic} connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the higher rank group $G=G_2'$ that are neither $\iota$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichm\"uller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call \emph{$\alpha$-bundles} and \emph{$\beta$-bundles}, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $\beta$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_{\beta}$-Anosov and $\alpha$-bundles are $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $\sigma \in \{\alpha, \beta\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_{\sigma})$-manifold ${\mathscr{M}}_{\sigma}(\rho)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $\rho:\pi_1S\rightarrow G_2'$ associated to a $\sigma$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $\rho$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $\pi_1({\mathscr{M}}_{\sigma}(\rho))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $\rho$ in the space of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic.
item.dc:creator: Colin Davalo, Parker Evans

item.title: Uncomputable trisection invariants of 4-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2608.27811v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that two invariants of smooth 4-manifolds defined in terms of trisections are uncomputable: the trisection genus and the Kirby-Thompson L-invariant. That is, there does not exist an algorithm that takes as input a triangulated closed orientable 4-manifold and outputs one of these quantities. The result on the L-invariant resolves the second part of Problem 4.116 in the K3 problem list. In the same spirit, we show that the PL multisection genus of PL manifolds is uncomputable in dimensions at least four.
item.dc:creator: Nathan M. Dunfield, Marc Kegel, Shana Yunsheng Li, Qiuyu Ren

item.title: One internal stabilization is enough for resolving self-referential tubes
item.description: arXiv:2609.29854v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper shows that one internal stabilization is enough to resolve all the self-referential tubes on an embedding. As an application, this paper gives a complete isotopy classification for embedded surfaces with a common geometric dual in orientable $S^2$-bundle over a surface, provided that the embedded surfaces have greater genus than the base surface of the bundle.
item.dc:creator: Qizheng You

item.title: Khovanov and knot Floer homology of fibered positive links
item.description: arXiv:2610.16539v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For fibered positive links, we compute the reduced and unreduced Khovanov homology in homological grading two over both $\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{F}_2$, and the knot Floer homology in the penultimate Alexander grading. Our Khovanov calculations, combined with the result of Przytycki-Sazdanovi\'c, prove that every nontrivial semi-adequate knot has 2-torsion in its unreduced Khovanov homology. This establishes Shumakovitch's conjecture for semi-adequate knots, which include all nontrivial positive knots. The proofs involve induction using the skein exact sequences, with the Hopf link as the base case.
item.dc:creator: Zhechi Cheng

item.title: Classifiyng metrically conical rational singularities
item.description: arXiv:1112.0125v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We will in this article classify which rational complex surface singularities are metrically conical, that is have the bilipschitz type of their inner metric equivalent to that of a cone. This is done using the thick-thin decomposition for the inner geometry of a normal complex surface singularity and properties of rational singularities. The result is a family of singularities depending only on their topology which is given as a $3$-parameter family.
item.dc:creator: Helge M{\o}ller Pedersen

item.title: Monodromy and vanishing cycles for complete intersection curves
item.description: arXiv:2408.06479v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compute the topological monodromy of every family of complete intersection curves. Like in the case of plane curves previously treated by the second-named author, we find the answer is given by the $r$-spin mapping class group associated to the maximal root of the adjoint line bundle. Our main innovation is a suite of tools for studying the monodromy of sections of a tensor product of very ample line bundles in terms of the monodromy of sections of the factors, allowing for an induction on (multi-)degree.
item.dc:creator: Ishan Banerjee, Nick Salter

item.title: Vietoris-Rips complexes of affine Coxeter groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.38703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that all affine Coxeter groups admit contractible Vietoris-Rips complexes. More precisely, for any affine Coxeter group $W_a$ with standard generating set $S$, we prove that the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathcal{VR}_t(W_a;S)$ is contractible for all sufficiently large $t$. We also investigate other finitely generated groups of the form $G=H\rtimes F$ for $F$ finite, and prove that for any finite symmetric generating set $A$ for $H$ such that $A^F=A$, the complexes $\mathcal{VR}_t(G;AF)$ and $\mathcal{VR}_t(H;A)$ are homotopy equivalent for all $t\ge 1$.
item.dc:creator: Riley Decker, Matthew C. B. Zaremsky

item.title: Generalized Hopf bifurcations: a homological analysis and obstructions to their existence
item.description: arXiv:2611.08002v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A generalized Hopf bifurcation takes place when varying a parameter of a (semi)dynamical system causes an attractor $K$ to become a repeller. In doing so, it expels a (parameter-dependent) family of attractors. In this paper we concentrate on two questions: (1) what do the expelled attractors look like?, and (2) can any attractor $K$ undergo a generalized Hopf bifurcation? Regarding (1), we compute the cohomology of the expelled attractors in terms of the cohomology of $K$; in the case of continuous-time dynamics this can be improved to a computation of their Borsuk shape. As for (2), we show that certain compacta cannot undergo generalized Hopf bifurcations and, when the ambient space has dimension $ \leq 3$, give a complete topological characterization of which can.
item.dc:creator: H\'ector Barge, J. J. S\'anchez-Gabites
